commit.message:
v1.91.19.0 fix: severe fix wave (truthful gates, no lost memory, every host finds gstack) (#3025)

* docs: approved severe fix wave plan (Oct 2026)

* D0: keep a project's .env and bunfig.toml out of compiled binaries and daemon children

Compiled binaries are built with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv and
--no-compile-autoload-bunfig; the browse server and terminal agent are
spawned with --no-env-file and an empty config, so a repo's .env cannot set
GSTACK_CHROMIUM_NO_SANDBOX and a bunfig preload cannot run code in them.
Verified on Bun 1.4.0.

* A9: --no-write is a dry run and leaves ingest state untouched

--no-write stamped every prepared page ingested_at and saved state, so a
later real run skipped those pages forever. It now prepares and reports
pages without importing or changing the state file.

Tests that used GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_NO_WRITE / --no-write to seed state
move to an explicit seam (a fake gbrain that accepts every staged page),
because the --no-write contract deliberately changes.

* H #2885 #2827: vector geometry is not phone or card PII

pii.phone.e164 accepts "." as a group separator, so a single float
(viewBox="0 0 581.66796875 ...") and a run of path coordinates
("37.6188 101.694") read as phone numbers. pii.cc's \b stops at a decimal
point, so the long fraction of an .excalidraw float is a Luhn candidate.
Excalidraw's seed/versionNonce/updated integers read as bare phone numbers.
A rendered /diagram triplet raised 18 (svg) and 97 (excalidraw) MEDIUM
findings on main; it now raises none.

- looksLikeDecimalCoordinates (ported from #2885, extended to a single
  decimal and refusing a leading "+", the E.164 marker)
- insideDecimalNumber: a cc span glued to "<digit>." or ".<digit>"
- isNumericMetadataValue: an unquoted JSON value under a seed, nonce or
  timestamp key; the same digits under "phone" still report

Controls: E.164 in prose, dotted and spaced phones, "+"-prefixed runs,
"phone"/"contact" JSON numbers, Luhn-valid cards in prose and at sentence end.

Co-authored-by: Lewis <lewispeel@hotmail.com>

* D1: pin the terminal-agent /ws Origin to the gstack extension (#1324)

GSTACK_EXTENSION_ID moves to browse/src/extension-id.ts, shared by
/extension-token and the terminal agent's /ws gate. /ws now returns 403 for
every origin except the pinned extension. Forks override the ID with
gstack-config set browse_extension_id <id>, honored by both routes; the
BROWSE_EXTENSION_ID env var is no longer read. Test sites that used fake
extension IDs now use the pinned origin.

* H #2899: env.kv skips a function call assigned to a credential name

`session = _FlakySession(...)`, `token = make_token(user, ...)` and
`password = getpass.getpass()` raised env.kv MEDIUM, which blocks the
fail-closed decision log. The exemption needs the line's evidence, not the
span's shape: the value is unquoted, is an identifier or dotted path
followed by "(", and the call closes on the line or opens a multi-line
argument list. Quoted values, unclosed "(" inside an unquoted secret
(API_SECRET=Abc123xyz(9Qm) and calls carrying a high-entropy literal
argument still report. The literal check is shared with the #2912 env-read
exemption.

Co-authored-by: Yugz <yannduzelier@gmail.com>

* H #2962: per-machine config filenames are not internal hostnames

`CLAUDE.local.md` and `settings.local.json` reported internal.hostname
MEDIUM (the pattern's \b stops at the dot before the extension), which fails
closed in the decision log. A span immediately followed by a known config
extension (.md .json .jsonc .yaml .yml .toml .ini .conf .txt) and a word
boundary is a filename. Controls: `ssh build.local`, `printer.local.` at a
sentence end, `printer.local/md`, `printer.local.mdx`, a host with a port,
`api.corp`, `build-7.internal`. The `.env.local` vectors (#2740) pass on
main already via isDotenvFilename and are pinned here as regressions.

Co-authored-by: Florian <florian.cleyetmerle@gmail.com>

* H #2784: four-part versions need a version declaration, not a shape

`"version": "1.128.1.0"`, `<Version>`, `AssemblyVersion("1.0.0.0")` and
Keep a Changelog headings raised pii.ip_public MEDIUM on every release,
because a four-part version is byte-for-byte a dotted quad. Exempt only when
the same line declares it a version immediately before the value (a version
key or word, an XML tag, an attribute call, or a `## [x]` heading). The same
digits after host:/server =/"upstream", bare on a line, or after prose that
merely mentions a version still report. Unlike #2784, this does not exempt a
value because the same string is declared a version elsewhere in the text:
that let a real address sharing a diff with a matching version slip. The
pre-push hook's VERSION-file rule (#2856) is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: cdecook23 <decook23@gmail.com>

* H #2913: postgres:postgres is exempt only on a loopback host

The postgres image's default pair in compose files and CI DATABASE_URLs
blocked pushes as db.url_with_password HIGH. It is now exempt only for
postgres/postgresql URLs with exactly postgres:postgres on localhost or
127.0.0.1 (optional port). A bare single-label host (`db`, `postgres`), any
other host, a host that merely starts with localhost (`localhost.evil...`,
`localhost@prod-db`), any other user or password, and other schemes still
block. #2913 exempted the pair on any host; this keeps the plan's narrower
rule.

Co-authored-by: mb1810 <michael.berger1810@gmail.com>

* G1: ship without a version when no version source is configured

Resolve the version source to four outcomes (valid, absent, ambiguous,
broken) in lib/version-source.ts and read that one signal in
gstack-version-bump (new NO_VERSION state; write refuses to invent a
VERSION), gstack-next-version (no_version, no slot), /ship's bump,
CHANGELOG and title steps, /land-and-deploy's drift check and
/document-release. A configured version file that is missing, empty,
unreadable or malformed stops with its path; 0.0.0.0 is never
substituted. docs/skills.md documents .gstack/version-path.

Migrates two tests that pinned the old fabricated-0.0.0.0 behavior.

Co-authored-by: Koda <koda@edgeviewfinance.com.au>
Co-authored-by: Merit Blake <merit@newsprint.com>

* H #2949: eval credential screen checks every name segment

The hermetic eval env admits GITHUB_* and EVALS_* metadata but rejects
credential-shaped names, judged only by the last underscore segment. A
trailing qualifier carried a credential through: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64,
GITHUB_TOKEN_1, EVALS_API_KEY_FALLBACK reached eval children. The screen
now rejects a name when any segment is a credential word; segments, not
substrings, so GITHUB_PATH / GITHUB_TOKENIZER / GITHUB_KEYRING stay
metadata, and explicit runner admissions still win.

Co-authored-by: Nguyen Thanh Dat <ntdat812@gmail.com>

* H #2915: cover chunked scanning of large multi-file push diffs

Test-only coverage for behavior already on main: a clean two-file pushed
diff over the engine's 1 MiB cap passes without engine.input_too_large, and
a credential at the end of the second file (a later scan chunk) still
blocks the push.

Co-authored-by: pneumorea-ai <pneumorea@gmail.com>

* A3: keep a project's DATABASE_URL away from a PGLite brain

With a PGLite config, buildGbrainEnv returned the caller env unchanged, so
a project's .env DATABASE_URL (autoloaded by Bun) reached gbrain: a false
broken-db at best, gbrain talking to the app's own Postgres at worst.
Inherited DATABASE_URL and GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL are now blanked for PGLite
configs (GSTACK_RESPECT_ENV_DATABASE_URL=1 still keeps them), and every
gbrain child runs from gbrain's config dir instead of the user's project,
so it cannot reload the project's .env / .env.local.

The old test that pinned pass-through for an engine:pglite config is
migrated: pass-through now applies only to configs that name neither a
database_url nor PGLite.

Co-authored-by: maxpetrusenkoagent <max.petrusenko.agent@gmail.com>

* C9: guard destructive gstack-upgrade and spec fences against unset or wrong paths

Fresh-shell hosts (and Claude Code, which keeps cwd but not shell variables)
ran cd "$INSTALL_DIR" with an empty variable, so git checkout/stash/reset
targeted the user's project. Step 2 now prints an absolute path; every
destructive fence starts with cd -- "${VAR:?...}" || exit 1 and checks it is
gstack's own checkout before any git command. /spec's worktree and spawn
fences get the same guard.

* F4: keep every paid design variant across regenerate rounds

$D variants now reserves a collision-safe round-<N>/ directory per run
(atomic mkdir) and writes a manifest.json of what each round saved. The
paid image request and the local write retry separately: a write failure
retries the write (temp + rename) and, if the path stays unwritable,
keeps the bytes in the temp dir instead of buying the image again.
Responsive variants land in their round directory too.

Readers updated: design-shotgun reserves a round dir and a private temp
dir for its parallel agents and records approved_path/round in
approved.json; design-html resolves approved_path (legacy letters still
work) and finds round-dir variants; design-consultation checks the
printed paths; the gallery shows round-dir variants. Variants that were
already overwritten before this change cannot be recovered.

Migrates the consultation contract test that pinned the flat path.

Co-authored-by: Matt Van Horn <mvanhorn@gmail.com>

* A2: stage dot-leading slugs gbrain can collect; network errors are db-unreachable

A page slug segment starting with a dot (a .claude project) staged a file
gbrain's import walker prunes, so the batch was refused on every run.
Leading dots become "dot-" per segment, and slugs recorded in state under
the old name map through the same function so no page is duplicated.

A DNS or connection failure (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNREFUSED, ...) no
longer classifies as broken-db, which routed users to move a working
config aside. The new db-unreachable status carries the reason
"database host unreachable (<code> <host>); your gbrain config is
unchanged. Fix: check network or VPN, then re-run /sync-gbrain.", skips
local sync stages with that reason, and counts as usable for
gstack-gbrain-detect --is-ok like timeout.

Co-authored-by: Infiniteyieldai <infiniteyield.ai@gmail.com>

* D2: one address classifier for navigation literals, DNS answers, redirects and page-driven navigations (#2811)

classifyAddress() in url-validation.ts blocks 169.254.0.0/16 (metadata and
container credential endpoints), 100.100.100.200, fe80::/10 and fc00::/7,
including IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible and NAT64 spellings and decimal,
octal and hex IPv4. validateNavigationUrl, the A/AAAA answer check and
session-persist's cookie-domain guard all use it. BrowserManager now checks
every navigation request (redirect hops, link clicks, scripted navigations):
a blocked target resets the tab to about:blank and the write command fails
with the reason. Connection-time DNS rebinding remains out of scope.

Co-authored-by: Gabriel Rondon <grondon@gmail.com>

* C4: external hosts point at carved sections relative to the installed skill

Publishes the pointer form setup matches: on every non-Claude host a carved
section is `sections/<file>` relative to the installed gstack-<skill> SKILL.md
directory (QA's existing form), never $GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections/, which
does not exist in external runtime roots. No render changes yet: only QA is
carved on external hosts today.

* INV-1: gate outcome contract for outside reviews

classifyOutsideReview() returns separate execution, findings and verdict
fields from text, stderr and exit status; reason codes, anchors and fix
actions live in lib/gate-outcomes.ts. validateOutsideReview() stays as the
text-only wrapper and the two-argument CLI keeps exit 0/1/2 for importers
and installed skills that predate a re-render. The --verdict form (implied
by --stderr/--exit) prints VERDICT/FINDINGS/REASON and exits 0/3/4/1; the
generated outside-voice caller moves to it and branches on each status
(unverified prints OUTSIDE_STATUS: unverified, never completed).

Adds docs/troubleshooting.md with one anchored section per reason code, the
anchor test, and the gate-tail lint (query scripts may not swallow failures,
gate calls may not end in || true, other best-effort tails say why).

* G1: quote the base placeholder in document-release title sync

The title-sync block is checked with bash -n; an unquoted <base> parses
as a redirection. Migrates the test that pinned the old root VERSION
read to the shared classifier call.

* G3: give every logging-bin mktemp a ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} template

Bare mktemp, mktemp -t and literal /tmp templates in the learnings,
question and preference logs (plus jsonl-merge, distill, the two
dashboards, /ship's PR body and /document-release's run dir) now use
"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>.XXXXXX", the form the INV-3 lint accepts. When
the temp file cannot be created, the learnings, question and preference
logs now say the entry was not recorded and how to fix TMPDIR instead of
exiting with only mktemp's own error. Three tests that pinned the bare
PR_BODY_FILE=$(mktemp) and one that pinned the /tmp run dir migrate.

GNU and BSD mktemp already honor TMPDIR without a template, so the
macOS-sandbox drop in #2952 is unverified here; the template makes the
temp location explicit on every mktemp.

Co-authored-by: Davon Johnson <d.johnson@dayofshow.net>

* B1b: structured outside-review gate fails on P0 as well as P1

validateOutsideReview() derived its structured pass/fail from a [P1] match,
so a review reporting only [P0] findings passed. The wrapper now reads the
classifier's findings verdict (P0 or P1), and the /review and /ship
structured-gate prose requests [P0]-[P3] tags and fails on P0/P1; untagged
output (OUTSIDE_STATUS: unverified) is missing coverage. The ship clarity
pin moves from 'structured P1' to 'structured P0/P1' with the behavior.

* E1: freeze normalizes boundary and target the same way on Windows; hooks spawn through cmd.exe (#2876, #2354)

gstack_hook_normalize_path (careful/bin/hook-extract.sh) maps C:\..., c:/...,
UNC \\server\share (leading // kept) and /cygdrive/c to one form; check-freeze
runs both the saved boundary and file_path through it before the absolute
test, after symlink resolution, and compares case-insensitively on Windows
bash. freeze, guard and careful register hooks as
bash -c "exec bash \"$HOME/...\"" so cmd.exe, which never expands $HOME,
no longer turns the hook into a silent exit 127.

Co-authored-by: Kevin Grasso <kevin@biblingo.com>
Co-authored-by: Xuan-Ce Wang <261591073+xwang4-svg@users.noreply.github.com>

* G4: keep CLI-to-daemon loopback calls off HTTP_PROXY (#494)

The CLI appends 127.0.0.1, localhost and ::1 to the user's NO_PROXY (and
no_proxy), keeping existing entries, before its first fetch. Verified on
Bun 1.4.0: fetch honors NO_PROXY when it is set before the first request
and ignores later changes, so it is set at the top of main().

* F1: bind the plan audit to this branch's plan, never the newest file

Plan File Discovery now prefers an explicit binding (the plan-mode file
or /autoplan ACTIVE_PLAN from the conversation, then a "Plan: <path>"
line in the PR body), then lists candidates: repo-committed
docs/designs/ files this branch changed or that name it, and personal
plan files that name the branch. Candidates are offered, never picked
silently. The repo-name match and the newest-file-of-the-day fallback,
which audited PRs against unrelated plans, are gone. With nothing bound
or chosen it prints the exact line 'Plan completion audit: not run (...).
Fix: add "Plan: <path>" to the PR body, or run /autoplan.'

/ship's parent now binds the plan before dispatching the audit
subagent ({{PLAN_COMPLETION_GATE_SHIP:discovery}}), so the child never
searches. Migrates three tests that pinned the old markers and notice.

Co-authored-by: loulanyue <260355617@qq.com>

* G5: browse type --selector <sel> <text> (#2936)

--selector focuses the element (sel or @ref) and types into it. The bare
form still types its text literally into the focused element; text that
starts with -- goes after a -- separator. When the first word looks like a
CSS selector, the result adds a hint to use --selector without echoing the
typed text, and never refuses based on page contents. Help and command
usage updated.

Co-authored-by: Thomas Reuser <thomasreuser@gmail.com>

* F2: design-doc discovery reads docs/designs, never a root DESIGN.md

A root DESIGN.md is the design system /design-consultation writes, so
preferring it unconditionally reviewed plans against a token file while
printing "Design doc found" and never looked at docs/designs/ feature
docs. Discovery now considers only docs/designs/*.md as the repo-local
design doc (still freshness-compared with the private ~/.gstack copy).
The CEO finding fixture seeds its supplied design as a docs/designs doc
and its test follows.

Co-authored-by: Bit0ps <alex.dreamscaper@gmail.com>

* C4: rename the external carve test (typecheck:test union-order artifact)

tsc prints a union's members in type-creation order; a test file sorting
before ceo-mode-option.test.ts reordered one baseline diagnostic's text.

* C1: every env-var host fence resolves its own gstack root

Codex and the other env-var hosts run each block in a fresh shell, so
GSTACK_ROOT/BIN, B and D set by the preamble were empty in later blocks
(/bin/gstack-slug, B=/browse). scripts/resolvers/runtime-root.ts now owns
root resolution: a valid exported GSTACK_ROOT (bin/ and lib/), else the
per-install literal root (no git call), else repo-local, else the global root
(CODEX_HOME on Codex); no root prints the setup fix line and exits. One
post-render pass inserts it (<=400 bytes) into every fence that uses these
variables without assigning them; B/D come from the same helper as BROWSE
and DESIGN SETUP. Claude output is byte-identical.

Migrated pins of the old preamble lines (gen-skill-docs.test.ts) and a
fixture whose exported GSTACK_ROOT lacked lib/ (skill-positional-literals).

* E8: headless browse honors GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH; extensions load in new headless mode (#2771, #1968, #2281)

The headless launch passes GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH as executablePath, scopes
the XProtect self-heal out for that bundle, and names the path in a launch
failure with the fix. BROWSE_EXTENSIONS_DIR now launches a persistent
context under the project state dir with --headless=new, so the extension
runs and no window appears (the off-screen window was visible on macOS and
the extension never ran in an isolated newContext). The GPU source guard
test moves from the removed useHeadless flag to launch() vs launchHeaded().

Co-authored-by: oli548 <312288720+oli548@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Slava <slava.istomin@tuta.io>
Co-authored-by: ryanlaiwy <129729476+ryanlaiwy@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: 李翊楠 <yinanli1917@gmail.com>

* C2: link design/dist and make-pdf/dist into every host runtime root and the agents sidecar

Codex design and make-pdf skills fall back to $GSTACK_DESIGN and
$GSTACK_MAKE_PDF under the runtime root, but setup linked only browse/dist,
so both preflights reported NOT_AVAILABLE on a fresh install. One helper
links dist/ only (make-pdf/ ships a Claude SKILL.md) into the Codex,
Factory, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot and Kiro roots, the .agents sidecar and
the Cursor sidecar.

Co-authored-by: Mammad M. <mammad@digit.az>

* C3: install router and nested SKILL.md files as real copies; back up hand edits; --status checks

Codex skips a symlinked SKILL.md file, so the gstack router linked into
~/.codex/skills/gstack was invisible. Every host runtime root (Codex,
Factory, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro) and Kiro's per-skill installs
now get real copies, rewritten on every run (the auto-update path runs
setup --refresh-registered, so it refreshes them too). setup records each
copy's hash in <state root>/skill-copies.tsv; a copy that no longer matches
is saved to a uniquely named backup under <state root>/backups/skill-copies/
before _activate_runtime_root replaces the tree, and a failed backup keeps
the old tree. setup prints what it refreshed or removed.

./setup --status now prints, per registered install, whether the router is a
real file and whether every section pointer resolves, with the fix command.

Test migration: setup-codex-model pinned the Kiro router/upgrade links as
_link_or_copy; C3 deliberately changes them to copies.

* INV-3: install-level host conformance checks (no symlinked SKILL.md, dist present, section pointers resolve)

For codex, kiro, factory, opencode, cursor and copilot, the real-setup
conformance kit now fails when an installed SKILL.md is a symlink, when
design/dist or make-pdf/dist is missing from the runtime root, or when a
'Read `.../sections/<f>.md`' pointer in an installed SKILL.md does not
resolve (bare pointers in carved skills, relative-to-installed-skill
pointers, and $GSTACK_ROOT/~/absolute/../ pointers everywhere), and
./setup --status must report 'all resolve'. No new setup runs.

Expected red until the generator lane lands: design-html's install-offer
pointer and plan-eng-review's review-sections pointer name
$GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections/... on every external host.

* B11: auto-update tracks pull, setup and migrations; announces only on success; retries with backoff

gstack-session-update wrote the 'just upgraded' marker after SETUP_FAILED or
SETUP_SKIPPED bun_missing, and re-ran setup only when HEAD moved, so a failed
install was announced as an upgrade and never retried. Stages are now
persisted in <state root>/session-update-pending; the marker is written only
when every stage succeeded; a pending setup or migrations stage is retried
even with HEAD unchanged after the update-check interval, then 6h, then 24h;
and each session start prints one line naming the stage, the reason and the
repair command while it is pending. Best-effort tails carry a same-line
reason.

* D1: gstack-config key browse_extension_id for forks and self-built extensions

The browse daemon trusts one Chrome extension ID on /extension-token and the
terminal-agent /ws. The override now lives only in gstack-config (never an
env var a project .env could set): empty by default (gstack's published
extension), a 32-letter a-p Chrome ID when set, "" clears it, and anything
else is rejected with the stored value kept. The browse lane reads it.

gstack-config-defaults: browse/src counts as a reader directory; the key is
listed prose-only until the browse lane's reader lands (the stale-entry check
then asks for the entry's removal).

* G2: key the sticky slug cache on the git common dir

A linked worktree used to resolve its slug fresh from the remote while
the main checkout kept its sticky pre-remote identity, so learnings,
checkpoints and timelines split into two buckets. gstack-slug and its
TS twin in lib/bin-context.ts now key the cache on the git common dir
(read from .git files, no git spawn, so cache hits stay git-free) and
read entries in one deterministic order: the repository entry, then the
main checkout's pre-upgrade entry, then this directory's own. Both the
repository and per-path entries are written.

When a worktree's own old entry named a different bucket that still
holds data, that slug is recorded in projects/<slug>/.former-slugs and
reported by --get FORMER_SLUGS. New --adopt-legacy --from <slug> merges
it: JSONL logs append missing lines with de-duplication, missing files
copy, differing files are listed as conflicts and never overwritten,
the source bucket is kept, and it prints migrated/pending/conflicting
counts; reruns are idempotent. --adopt-legacy --dismiss <slug> drops
the reminder.

Co-authored-by: loulanyue <260355617@qq.com>

* C5: OpenCode /gstack-* commands load the skill by its frontmatter name

OpenCode's skill tool knows gstack-review as `review` (its frontmatter
name), and OpenCode's builtin /review shadows that name as a command. The
managed /gstack-review command told the agent to load `gstack-review`,
a name the skill tool does not list. Every managed command now names the
frontmatter name. OpenCode's AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode mapping (#2759)
already shipped in v1.91.16.0.

Test migration: the #2629 commands test pinned the directory name.

Co-authored-by: Lockyer <135391289+Lockyer228@users.noreply.github.com>

* E4: Windows node-server bundle keeps sharp and socks external; CLI resolves its server script lazily (#2260, #2439)

build-node-server.sh passes --external sharp and --external socks (Bun on
Windows refuses to inline them; on Linux they were silently inlined). The
CLI no longer resolves server.ts or server-node.mjs at module load:
resolveServerLaunch() runs when a server starts, so a Windows minimal
runtime with only server-node.mjs works and a missing script is reported
only when one is needed.

Co-authored-by: Spooks444 <193448029+Spooks444@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: punksterlabs <77217235+punksterlabs@users.noreply.github.com>

* B1: Codex reviews whose sandbox could not start are unavailable, not a pass

In containers without unprivileged user namespaces every Codex command
fails, yet the review exits 0 and concludes 'no findings' (captured in
test/fixtures/codex-sandbox/). The validator now takes execution evidence:
'codex exec --json' command events and the 'codex review' stderr transcript
(a command that succeeded proves execution); sandbox failure lines on
stderr or in failed command output return unavailable(sandbox_unavailable);
exact 'could not run commands / read the diff' phrases are the last
fallback. Review text that merely discusses bwrap or namespaces still passes.

A free 'codex sandbox ... true' preflight (Linux, 10 s) runs before the paid
model probe and every automatic outside review; CODEX_MODE gains
sandbox_unavailable, and an inconclusive model probe reports unverified
instead of ready (exit code kept for stale callers). Every Codex site
(outside-voice resolver, /codex review, challenge, consult) takes its sandbox
from _GSTACK_CODEX_SANDBOX and pipes its result through the validator; a
static test parses rendered command positions for both. GSTACK_CODEX_NO_SANDBOX=1
(exactly 1, shell env only) switches to danger-full-access with a warning on
every use. Sandbox pins in existing tests move from the literal read-only to
the selected-sandbox variable; captured autoplan probes are judged against
the probe block they executed.

* C6: gstack-relink discovers skills structurally, so /browse survives a skill_prefix toggle

relink skipped a hardcoded list of support-directory names that included
browse, a real skill, so toggling skill_prefix removed /browse. A top-level
directory is now a skill exactly when it carries a SKILL.md.

Co-authored-by: Jonathan Zhang <topcoder1@Mac-Studio.local>

* C4: carve ship and plan-ceo-review on every host; enforce the 160 KB byte gate

The generated ship skill was 202-241 KB on all 10 non-Claude hosts (and
Factory plan-ceo-review 160,039 bytes), over the 160,000-byte ceiling,
because section carving ran only for Claude. Both skills now carve on every
host, pointing at sections relative to the installed skill directory (literal
$GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections refs are rewritten the same way). The ceiling
is measured in UTF-8 bytes and fails generation in repo mode; under
--install-root it warns so setup never leaves a user without skills.

qa-lazy-sections.test.ts pinned ship as inline-on-external-hosts; migrated to
the carved policy and kept the inline check on review (Claude-only carve).

* B5: learnings and timeline reads fail loudly when bun is missing

gstack-learnings-search and gstack-timeline-read ended in
'2>/dev/null || exit 0', so a missing bun or a crashed embedded script
printed nothing and exited 0, identical to 'nothing recorded'. Both now
exit 127 with '<script>: bun not found on PATH, so ... could not be
read. Fix: install Bun (https://bun.sh), then re-run ./setup.' and let
an embedded-script failure exit non-zero with its stderr. A successful
run with no matches still exits 0 with empty output. The generated
callers that print 'LEARNINGS: unavailable (...)' belong to the
generator lane.

Co-authored-by: loulanyue <260355617@qq.com>

* B2: a retired-model 404 reports MODEL_UNUSABLE, not CODEX_MODE: ready

The model probe matched only 400 / 'is not supported', so a retired model's
404 ('does not exist or you do not have access to it') and a custom
provider's bare 404 fell through to the inconclusive branch and reported
ready. Both now classify as MODEL_UNUSABLE with a hint naming the two causes
(retired model, or a wrong base_url) and log codex_model_retired; a
'requires a newer version of Codex' 400 points at upgrading the CLI and logs
codex_cli_outdated. Ported from #2843 onto the current probe.

Co-authored-by: Marek Cermak <marek.cermak@strv.com>

* B6: rank learnings by matched query tokens and disclose truncation

A more specific query used to drop the exact match: the token-OR filter
recalled every entry sharing one token, the sort used confidence alone,
and the default --limit cut silently. Entries now rank by how many
distinct query tokens they match, then confidence, then recency, and a
query that matched more than fit says '-- N more matched, raise --limit
to see them'. The hit count lives in a local map so a field stored on
disk can never become a sort key, and the type grouping uses a
null-prototype map so a row typed 'constructor' or '__proto__' cannot
crash the run. Ranking code ported from #2796; regression vectors
adapted from #2799 (its stemmer is not needed).

Co-authored-by: y$un_ <forrest.sun527@gmail.com>

Copilot CLI applies Claude-format matchers by tool name; its skill tool is
`skill`, which no Claude tool name maps to, so the 'Skill' matcher never
fired and Copilot ran protected skills without gstack. The hook entry now
matches 'Skill|skill', an entry an older team-init wrote is upgraded in

working self-hosted or OpenAI-compatible provider configured with
[model_providers.<id>] env_key = "X" reported AUTH_FAILED and /codex

* B10: plan-tune never reports CALIBRATED with zero signal events

Stats printed CALIBRATED: true from logged-answer counts alone, while
every answer could miss SIGNAL_MAP and leave each dimension at its 0.5
seed (#2623). --derive now records inferred.signal_events, the answers

the summary prints 'not calibrated: no recorded signals' verbatim when
there are none (or says the count is unknown for a profile derived
before this change). The psychographic redesign stays out of scope.

* A1: verify gbrain landing before stamping transcripts, plus --reconcile

gbrain import exits 0 while skipping pages (returned per-file failures,
malformed filenames, managed-import Pending receipts), and its failure
ledger exists only for git import dirs, so a skipped page was stamped
ingested and never retried (field reports: 37 and 69 lost entries).

Write, verify, then stamp (lib/memory-ingest-landing.ts, a new ratcheted
module):
- State schema 2 with a transition table (staged -> imported_unverified ->
  ingested, plus refused, quarantined, unrecoverable). Schema 1 files
  migrate in place: entries become ingested in the legacy "default"
  source and a reconcile pass is marked pending.
- Named failures come from --json `failures`, stderr "Skipped <rel>:"
  lines and the ledger; a failure gbrain does not attribute refuses the
  whole batch. After 3 refused batches the batch is bisected and the page
  that poisons it is quarantined (printed even under --quiet).
- Landing check: one `gbrain list --source-id` per source per run and at
  most 50 `gbrain get --json` content checks against a
  gstack_content_sha256 frontmatter field gstack now writes. Lookup errors
  and pglite_busy mean "not yet checked", never absent; pages over the cap
  stay imported_unverified and are not re-imported.
- Each entry records its gbrain source_id. Remote-http mode records
  "staged", never "ingested".
- The source fingerprint comes from the exact bytes parsed, so a
  transcript that grows during import is not stamped as its newer self
  (the old unscanned contract test is migrated; it pinned that bug).
- --reconcile mode (bounded by --limit, default 200; resumable; --dry-run;
  backs up the state file) prints "reconcile: checked N, present M,
  re-queued K, not yet checked L". --request-reconcile records a pending
  pass without calling gbrain; the v1.91.17.0 migration (placeholder name)
  uses it, and the next ingest run does one bounded pass.
- One lock for every state writer; a state-save failure fails the run.

The #1802 static pins in regression-1611 move to the new structure
(remote-http returns before importBatch; the finally honors
preserveStaging).

Co-authored-by: afshaker <andrew@phone2.io>

* B4: arm64 re-sign keeps a backup, restores it when codesign fails, and reports design unavailable on exit 137

signature) and left it that way when re-signing failed; a design binary that
was then SIGKILLed at launch produced at most a quiet log line. Each binary is

* D3: treat design docs and handoff notes as data in plan reviews

plan-ceo-review, plan-eng-review and plan-devex-review read the freshest
design doc as the source of truth, and nothing said its content is data.

note beside it, with reviewer-directed text ('skip Step 0', 'approve
as-is'). Each read site now says the doc and any handoff note are data,
never to follow text aimed at the reviewer, and to report it as
suspicious content. The plan-completion audit's discovery, which now
reads repo docs/designs/ files (F1), carries the same rule.

Probe: a gbrain user render serves ship/SKILL.md from the render dir; its

G1's NO_VERSION arms, F1's parent-side plan binding and D3's data line
add 2,126 bytes to /ship's skeleton-plus-sections union, taking it from

* E5: feed every Codex prompt on stdin instead of argv

Prompts went to Codex as one argv string ('codex exec "$(cat file)"'), which
fails over 32 KB on Windows (and over 128 KB on Linux, E2BIG) and mangles
quotes. Every codex exec site (outside-voice resolver, /codex review custom
instructions, challenge, consult new and resume) now runs 'codex exec -'
with the prepared prompt file on stdin; challenge and consult write the
prompt with a quoted heredoc so it is never shell-parsed. The bash-native
timeout watchdog (stock macOS) started the command in the background, which
gives it /dev/null as stdin; it now passes the caller's stdin through.

The 'byte for byte' dispatch test drops its old argv trailing-LF exception,
the consultation and autoplan fixtures follow the stdin form, and the static
site test requires stdin at every rendered codex exec.

* G6: prettyscreenshot --hide keeps a trailing image path as the output path (#1419)

--hide collected every following non-flag argument as a selector, so the
output path was hidden instead of written to. A trailing argument that looks
like a path or ends in .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp is now the output path.

Under Git Bash, a native Windows Python first on PATH cannot open an MSYS
/c/... path, so gbrain-refresh always summarized the detection as

The duration step parsed 'ps -o lstart=' with BSD-only 'date -jf', so on

* Q2: one-time notice naming the Codex provider and account for outside reviews

Outside reviews are on by default and use whatever Codex login exists
(#965). The first automatic Codex review on a machine now prints one
non-blocking notice: the provider (config.toml model_provider, else openai),
where the credential comes from (CODEX_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, the ChatGPT
login or the key saved by codex login; never the value), that reviews stay
on, and how to turn them off (gstack-config set codex_reviews disabled). A

the generated command now use private state roots. Also shortens the
no-sandbox provenance line.

validateOutputPath walks the destination one component at a time, resolving
each existing component before the next, so link/../x, a dangling symlink
and a dangling symlinked parent can no longer route a write outside the
safe directories, while a new multi-level directory inside them is allowed.
scrape validates its manifest and every downloaded file, not only --dir.
Ported from PR #2971 onto current code.

(test_*.py|rb), XCTest (Tests/ dirs, FooTests.swift), Terraform
(*.tftest.hcl) and Bats (*.bats) suites counted as zero, and a committed

LOC). is_test now knows those conventions and never treats prose as a
test, generated output is skipped in the numstat pass, TEST_FILES_CHANGED
uses is_test, and TEST_FILES_TOTAL uses the same filename conventions
minus generated paths. Merges #2812, #2809 and #2037's patterns (#2037's

* E5: watchdog stdin test feeds the wrapper through a redirect

Callers run '_gstack_codex_timeout_wrapper ... codex exec - < file'. Bash keeps
stdin for a backgrounded command inside a pipeline but not behind a
redirect, so the pipe form passed on the old watchdog; the redirect form
reproduces the lost prompt.

typeof fetch; it now takes the fetch arguments like

* A4: import transcripts into per-repository, non-federated gbrain sources

`gbrain import` ran without --source-id, so transcripts from every project
landed in the shared (often federated) default source.

- Each transcript partition imports with --source-id into its originating
  repository's own source (gstack-transcripts-<repo>, built with
  constrainSourceId, now exported from lib/gbrain-sources.ts). The source
  is registered machine-local and --no-federated before its first import,
  and the registration is cached in state. Partitions import one after
  another (PGLite is a single writer); a failing source no longer blocks
  the others, except a timeout, whose checkpoint must survive.
- If gbrain cannot register the source, that partition stays local and
  unstamped, and the run says why (even under --quiet).
- --include-unattributed sends repo-less transcripts only to the
  machine-local gstack-transcripts-unattributed source, keeps them on the
  machine when the brain is remote (Postgres, Supabase or remote-HTTP),
  and never writes them to the publishable ~/.gstack/transcripts staging.
- A page's recorded source is sticky: pages stamped before this release
  ("default") keep importing there, so no source gains a duplicate.
- The staging dir name carries -src-<id> so a resumed import keeps its
  source.

Test fakes that recorded only the last import now record every import of
one run, and answer `gbrain sources`; remote-http scan tests use an
attributed transcript, since unattributed ones no longer stage there.

The taste-profile probe double-quoted ~/.claude/.../gstack-slug, so the tilde

DESIGN SETUP (and office-hours' visual exploration) printed DESIGN_READY for
any executable binary, so one SIGKILLed at launch by an invalid macOS code
signature still passed. Launch it under the portable 10-second deadline
(gtimeout, timeout, or perl alarm); otherwise print DESIGN_NOT_AVAILABLE with
the exit code, 'timed out after 10s', or on 137 the code-signature hint and

The generator lane's C1 resolves D from $GSTACK_ROOT instead of
$GSTACK_DESIGN, so the test now exports GSTACK_ROOT as well; it still fails
on main (no dist in the roots) and passes with and without the C1 change.

* A5: brain-sync stage fails loud when the artifacts source indexed zero pages

The stage reported "curated artifacts pushed" whenever gstack-brain-sync
exited 0, but a git push is not gbrain indexing. After a successful push
the stage now reads the maintained artifacts source's page count

Co-authored-by: Jimmy Zeisweiss <4261258+jzeisweiss@users.noreply.github.com>

* B1: state the effective read-only sandbox in /codex review prose

The codex parity invariant requires the skill to state sandbox_mode="read-only";
the command now takes it from _GSTACK_CODEX_SANDBOX, so the prose names the

* A6: report deleted-worktree gbrain sources; prune only with proof, on request

A deleted Conductor worktree leaves its gstack-code-<hash> source behind
and gbrain's autopilot fails on it forever. Local absence is not proof a
source is dead (machines sharing a federated brain register their own
paths, and its pages may be the only copy of uncommitted work), so gstack
never removes one automatically.

- Each sync counts consecutive misses for gstack code sources whose path
  is missing, prints "path unavailable" once per source with the review
  command, and records which repository each synced source belongs to.
- New gstack-gbrain-sync --prune-gone-worktrees (with --dry-run, whose
  plan it always prints first) removes a source only when its path was
  missing on two consecutive syncs, its parent is readable, recomputing
  deriveCodeSourceId() for that path on this host yields its id, and the
  repository's git common dir still exists and no longer lists the
  worktree. It re-checks the path right before removing (through the
  #1734-guarded safeSourcesRemove) and logs each removal.

* D0: pass the Bun child flags after 'run' so wrappers that rewrite 'bun run' argv keep working

bun run --no-env-file --config=/dev/null <script> has the same effect
(verified on Bun 1.4.0) and keeps argv[1] === 'run', which the
publication-lock fixture's preload injection relies on. The sidebar-tabs
source guard now expects the flags in the terminal-agent spawn.

* E8: count the BROWSE_EXTENSIONS_DIR persistent launch in the signal-flags guard

The new launch site carries handleSIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP false like the
other three, so the guard's expected count moves from 3 to 4.

* D2: give the memory-leak reproducer's fake request isNavigationRequest()

wirePageEvents now runs the navigation guard on every request event; the
fake request adapter supplies the method real Playwright requests have.

* A7: run only the resolve_symbol_edges dream phase, detected first

/sync-gbrain --dream and the --full auto-build ran gbrain's full dream
cycle (~35 minutes, LLM phases) when the call graph needs only the
resolve_symbol_edges phase. The stage now runs
gbrain dream [--source <id>] --phase resolve_symbol_edges when the
installed gbrain accepts that phase (detected by behavior: gbrain
validates --phase before printing --help). Otherwise it skips the forced
dream and says the full cycle costs about 35 minutes and how to run it,
instead of starting it.

PR body Pre-Landing Review section and /review's completion rule now say

repo edit, which always fails (gh wants [HOST/]OWNER/REPO), then step 2
rewrote ~/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt to the never-renamed repository.

* B8: read gbrain JSON with bun instead of jq in install and wireup

gstack-gbrain-install read package.json with jq but never checked for it,
so on a machine without jq a successful install failed with "cannot read
version". gstack-gbrain-source-wireup hard-failed without jq ("brew
install jq" is not actionable on git-bash), so the wireup was skipped on
every run. Both now read the JSON with bun, which they already require.

Co-authored-by: benjamin beres <benjamin.beres@bienpreter.com>

* B4: shorter probe messages (design-consultation parity budget)

* B5: shorter capture variable names (parity budget)

* E7: find the Aside CLI in ~/.local/bin when it is not on PATH (#2902)

The installer puts aside in ~/.local/bin, which is not on the default macOS
login PATH, so the probe said NEEDS_ASIDE ('download Aside') for a healthy
install. The probe now falls back to ~/.local/bin/aside, drives the resolved
binary, and prints READY: <path> when it is off PATH so later blocks run that
path. Ported from PR #2965 onto the current _gs_d probe.

Co-authored-by: Som Samantray <som.samantray@gmail.com>

* A2: key the dot-slug catalog entry on the message users actually saw

* E1: cmd.exe-safe investigate freeze hook

On Windows Claude Code runs hook commands through cmd.exe, which cannot parse
the single-quoted bash -c argument, so /investigate's scope-lock hook never
ran. Use one double-quoted bash -c script that names the hook path directly
(no S= variable: POSIX sh would expand $S to empty and skip the hook).

* F4: design resolver reads per-round variant paths

$D variants now writes $_DESIGN_DIR/round-<N>/variant-*.png and prints JSON
with roundDir, manifest and paths. The mockup flow and comparison-board loops
build the board from those printed paths instead of hardcoded
variant-{A,B,C}.png, and approved.json records approved_path and round so a
round-1 choice made after round 2 still resolves.

* E4: generators tolerate Bun's spurious EEXIST on Windows (#2329)

Bun on Windows throws EEXIST from a recursive mkdir of an existing directory,
so gen:skill-docs and the llms.txt writer crashed once a second file landed
in a directory. Both now use lib/fs-utils' mkdirpSync (ported from PR #2329
onto the existing helper instead of a new scripts/fs-utils.ts).

Co-authored-by: Vaughan <vaughan@cairnsitguy.com.au>

* C7: keep the required-mode hook's exit-2 deny

Copilot CLI treats a preToolUse exit 2 as deny (its hooks reference), and
#2413 established exit 2 plus hookSpecificOutput as the shape Claude Code
enforces, so the deny output stays as on main; only the matcher and the
in-place upgrade of older 'Skill' entries change.

* C3: guard Kiro's router copies on a present source; give the QA pointer adapter the copy and dist helpers

A copy fails where a symlink dangled, so the Kiro router and upgrade copies
are written only when their render exists (as every other runtime root
already does). test/qa-lazy-sections' extracted Kiro installer now supplies
_link_runtime_dists (C2) and the SKILL.md copy helpers (C3).

* Q3: office-hours asks open-ended questions in a Q<N> prose form (#2719)

In Conductor, and whenever AskUserQuestion fails, prose is the only channel,
and the prose fallback defined only the D<N> decision brief. Phase 2A/2B
diagnostic questions have no option set, so the model dropped the phase.
Office-hours' preamble now defines the Q<N> open-question form (question,
why I'm asking, what a strong answer sounds like) and routes free-text
replies to it; the diagnostic sections name it. Scoped to office-hours so
every other skill's preamble is unchanged. Ported from PR #2729.

Co-authored-by: Bharadwaj Mittapelli <bharadwajmittapelli@gmail.com>

* A2: render db-unreachable like timeout

gbrain's new db-unreachable status is a transient network failure; a setup
run while offline must not strip brain-aware blocks from every skill.

* A2: treat db-unreachable like timeout in gbrain-refresh

The memory lane's new db-unreachable status (network or DNS failure, config
intact) is transient, so gbrain-refresh keeps rendering brain-aware blocks
for it exactly as it does for timeout instead of suppressing them.

* C8: a render given disabled skills drops them from the router (#3018)

The root router named every skill and ends 'When in doubt, invoke the skill',
so it routed to skills the user disabled. gen-skill-docs takes
--disabled-skills (runGeneration disabledSkills): the router drops their
routing rules, keeps the other side of an 'A or B' rule, and names them as
disabled. The router and gstack-upgrade cannot be disabled. With no disabled
skills the render is byte-identical.

* G2/G3/INV-1: skill-start former-bucket notice and visible learnings failure; TMPDIR mktemp in gbrain bins; best-effort reasons

* C9: Step 2 falls back to the install registry's source checkout (DX-7)

Codex users who installed from the README's ~/gstack clone got 'ERROR:
gstack not found' from /gstack-upgrade: Step 2 only looked under host skill
directories. It now falls back to the source checkout the install registry
recorded for the current host.

* B4: design --version prints the version, and the probe uses it

The design CLI treated --version as an unknown command (exit 1), so the
probe launched the binary with no arguments instead. Add --version (prints
the gstack version, exit 0, before auth or network) and probe with it, so
messages read '<path> --version exited <code>' as planned.

* C4: no external render points at a section file that is not installed

design-html's detector install offer and plan-eng-review's self-check pointed
at $GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections/<file> on every external host, where neither
skill is carved and no section tree exists. design-html now inlines the offer
off Claude, and a skill's pointer to its own {{SECTION}}-inlined section
names the inlined text.

* C1: skillify finds the browse SDK under its own host's install root

The template hardcoded ~/.claude/skills/gstack for the canonical
browse-client.ts, so external hosts read another host's install or nothing.
A new INSTALLED_ROOT resolver (sibling of INSTALLED_BIN_DIR) names the host's
global root, or the per-install root when setup renders for one.

* C4: rewrite section refs on hosts whose root stays a literal ~/<globalRoot>

Kiro, OpenCode, Cursor and Copilot render ~/.claude/skills/gstack as their own
literal root, not $GSTACK_ROOT, so plan-eng-review's self-check pointer
escaped the rewrite (found by the setup lane's installed-pointer check).

* Integrator: outside-voice fences use the shared runtime prelude; TMPDIR mktemp and per-round variant paths in design templates

* Integrator: C8 router omits disabled skills on every render (relink renders the served Claude router in place); Windows-safe E4/E6 entries; investigate hooks under the cmd.exe check; browse_extension_id reader; order-insensitive test typecheck identities

tsc printed one unchanged ceo-mode-option diagnostic's object members in a
different order (content?/isError?) once lib/fs-utils joined the generator's
import graph; identities now sort object-type members, and old baselines
normalize on read.

* Q1 (#2971 salvage): bound iOS proxy responses

One wall-clock deadline covers headers and body (stalled and dribbling bodies
time out), the whole body is capped at 64 MiB (upstream_response_too_large),
every terminal path clears its timer, removes listeners and destroys the
request, and the daemon threads the deadline through both listeners. Ambiguous
mutations are still never replayed after a timeout or abort. Ported from
#2971's proxy-transport work plus the size bound.

* I1: grade the AUQ matrix's (recommended) marker on option labels, the field the auto-decide hook reads

The decision-brief format puts a Pros / cons block with 'A) ... (recommended)'
in the question text and the same marker on the option label. The matrix
counted both and failed all six skills in periodic run 37151477069 with
'expected exactly one (recommended) option, found 2'. The question-preference
hook reads labels only, so the gate now checks the native question: a
Recommendation line in the question text and exactly one label ending in
(recommended). Fixtures move to the native question shape and add the real
spec capture plus a marker-only-in-text negative control.

* Q1: type the proxy-transport test doubles (typecheck:test ratchet)

* INV-1: gate outcome rows and troubleshooting sections for every lane's new messages

* Release v1.91.19.0 (next free patch in the queue: #3022 holds 1.91.17.0, #3023 holds 1.91.18.0); migration renamed; engines.bun >=1.4.0 to match the CI pin (#2815)

Codex 0.160 refuses to create its helper aliases (codex-linux-sandbox among
them) when CODEX_HOME sits under its temp dir, and the runner put the
hermetic home under the shard TMPDIR. Periodic run 37151477069 shows the
warning and 'Unable to spawn codex-linux-sandbox ... No viable candidates
found in PATH' for every exec_command in codex-sol-scope-termination.

* I1: Codex evals fail a review whose commands never ran and stop reading tool errors as skill-load problems

validateCodexReview accepted codex-review-findings in periodic run 37151477069
although its only command failed in bwrap ('I could…

v1.91.19.0 fix: severe fix wave (truthful gates, no lost memory, every host finds gstack) (#3025)

* docs: approved severe fix wave plan (Oct 2026)

* D0: keep a project's .env and bunfig.toml out of compiled binaries and daemon children

Compiled binaries are built with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv and
--no-compile-autoload-bunfig; the browse server and terminal agent are
spawned with --no-env-file and an empty config, so a repo's .env cannot set
GSTACK_CHROMIUM_NO_SANDBOX and a bunfig preload cannot run code in them.
Verified on Bun 1.4.0.

* A9: --no-write is a dry run and leaves ingest state untouched

--no-write stamped every prepared page ingested_at and saved state, so a
later real run skipped those pages forever. It now prepares and reports
pages without importing or changing the state file.

Tests that used GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_NO_WRITE / --no-write to seed state
move to an explicit seam (a fake gbrain that accepts every staged page),
because the --no-write contract deliberately changes.

* H #2885 #2827: vector geometry is not phone or card PII

pii.phone.e164 accepts "." as a group separator, so a single float
(viewBox="0 0 581.66796875 ...") and a run of path coordinates
("37.6188 101.694") read as phone numbers. pii.cc's \b stops at a decimal
point, so the long fraction of an .excalidraw float is a Luhn candidate.
Excalidraw's seed/versionNonce/updated integers read as bare phone numbers.
A rendered /diagram triplet raised 18 (svg) and 97 (excalidraw) MEDIUM
findings on main; it now raises none.

- looksLikeDecimalCoordinates (ported from #2885, extended to a single
  decimal and refusing a leading "+", the E.164 marker)
- insideDecimalNumber: a cc span glued to "<digit>." or ".<digit>"
- isNumericMetadataValue: an unquoted JSON value under a seed, nonce or
  timestamp key; the same digits under "phone" still report

Controls: E.164 in prose, dotted and spaced phones, "+"-prefixed runs,
"phone"/"contact" JSON numbers, Luhn-valid cards in prose and at sentence end.

Co-authored-by: Lewis <lewispeel@hotmail.com>

* D1: pin the terminal-agent /ws Origin to the gstack extension (#1324)

GSTACK_EXTENSION_ID moves to browse/src/extension-id.ts, shared by
/extension-token and the terminal agent's /ws gate. /ws now returns 403 for
every origin except the pinned extension. Forks override the ID with
gstack-config set browse_extension_id <id>, honored by both routes; the
BROWSE_EXTENSION_ID env var is no longer read. Test sites that used fake
extension IDs now use the pinned origin.

* H #2899: env.kv skips a function call assigned to a credential name

`session = _FlakySession(...)`, `token = make_token(user, ...)` and
`password = getpass.getpass()` raised env.kv MEDIUM, which blocks the
fail-closed decision log. The exemption needs the line's evidence, not the
span's shape: the value is unquoted, is an identifier or dotted path
followed by "(", and the call closes on the line or opens a multi-line
argument list. Quoted values, unclosed "(" inside an unquoted secret
(API_SECRET=Abc123xyz(9Qm) and calls carrying a high-entropy literal
argument still report. The literal check is shared with the #2912 env-read
exemption.

Co-authored-by: Yugz <yannduzelier@gmail.com>

* H #2962: per-machine config filenames are not internal hostnames

`CLAUDE.local.md` and `settings.local.json` reported internal.hostname
MEDIUM (the pattern's \b stops at the dot before the extension), which fails
closed in the decision log. A span immediately followed by a known config
extension (.md .json .jsonc .yaml .yml .toml .ini .conf .txt) and a word
boundary is a filename. Controls: `ssh build.local`, `printer.local.` at a
sentence end, `printer.local/md`, `printer.local.mdx`, a host with a port,
`api.corp`, `build-7.internal`. The `.env.local` vectors (#2740) pass on
main already via isDotenvFilename and are pinned here as regressions.

Co-authored-by: Florian <florian.cleyetmerle@gmail.com>

* H #2784: four-part versions need a version declaration, not a shape

`"version": "1.128.1.0"`, `<Version>`, `AssemblyVersion("1.0.0.0")` and
Keep a Changelog headings raised pii.ip_public MEDIUM on every release,
because a four-part version is byte-for-byte a dotted quad. Exempt only when
the same line declares it a version immediately before the value (a version
key or word, an XML tag, an attribute call, or a `## [x]` heading). The same
digits after host:/server =/"upstream", bare on a line, or after prose that
merely mentions a version still report. Unlike #2784, this does not exempt a
value because the same string is declared a version elsewhere in the text:
that let a real address sharing a diff with a matching version slip. The
pre-push hook's VERSION-file rule (#2856) is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: cdecook23 <decook23@gmail.com>

* H #2913: postgres:postgres is exempt only on a loopback host

The postgres image's default pair in compose files and CI DATABASE_URLs
blocked pushes as db.url_with_password HIGH. It is now exempt only for
postgres/postgresql URLs with exactly postgres:postgres on localhost or
127.0.0.1 (optional port). A bare single-label host (`db`, `postgres`), any
other host, a host that merely starts with localhost (`localhost.evil...`,
`localhost@prod-db`), any other user or password, and other schemes still
block. #2913 exempted the pair on any host; this keeps the plan's narrower
rule.

Co-authored-by: mb1810 <michael.berger1810@gmail.com>

* G1: ship without a version when no version source is configured

Resolve the version source to four outcomes (valid, absent, ambiguous,
broken) in lib/version-source.ts and read that one signal in
gstack-version-bump (new NO_VERSION state; write refuses to invent a
VERSION), gstack-next-version (no_version, no slot), /ship's bump,
CHANGELOG and title steps, /land-and-deploy's drift check and
/document-release. A configured version file that is missing, empty,
unreadable or malformed stops with its path; 0.0.0.0 is never
substituted. docs/skills.md documents .gstack/version-path.

Migrates two tests that pinned the old fabricated-0.0.0.0 behavior.

Co-authored-by: Koda <koda@edgeviewfinance.com.au>
Co-authored-by: Merit Blake <merit@newsprint.com>

* H #2949: eval credential screen checks every name segment

The hermetic eval env admits GITHUB_* and EVALS_* metadata but rejects
credential-shaped names, judged only by the last underscore segment. A
trailing qualifier carried a credential through: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64,
GITHUB_TOKEN_1, EVALS_API_KEY_FALLBACK reached eval children. The screen
now rejects a name when any segment is a credential word; segments, not
substrings, so GITHUB_PATH / GITHUB_TOKENIZER / GITHUB_KEYRING stay
metadata, and explicit runner admissions still win.

Co-authored-by: Nguyen Thanh Dat <ntdat812@gmail.com>

* H #2915: cover chunked scanning of large multi-file push diffs

Test-only coverage for behavior already on main: a clean two-file pushed
diff over the engine's 1 MiB cap passes without engine.input_too_large, and
a credential at the end of the second file (a later scan chunk) still
blocks the push.

Co-authored-by: pneumorea-ai <pneumorea@gmail.com>

* A3: keep a project's DATABASE_URL away from a PGLite brain

With a PGLite config, buildGbrainEnv returned the caller env unchanged, so
a project's .env DATABASE_URL (autoloaded by Bun) reached gbrain: a false
broken-db at best, gbrain talking to the app's own Postgres at worst.
Inherited DATABASE_URL and GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL are now blanked for PGLite
configs (GSTACK_RESPECT_ENV_DATABASE_URL=1 still keeps them), and every
gbrain child runs from gbrain's config dir instead of the user's project,
so it cannot reload the project's .env / .env.local.

The old test that pinned pass-through for an engine:pglite config is
migrated: pass-through now applies only to configs that name neither a
database_url nor PGLite.

Co-authored-by: maxpetrusenkoagent <max.petrusenko.agent@gmail.com>

* C9: guard destructive gstack-upgrade and spec fences against unset or wrong paths

Fresh-shell hosts (and Claude Code, which keeps cwd but not shell variables)
ran cd "$INSTALL_DIR" with an empty variable, so git checkout/stash/reset
targeted the user's project. Step 2 now prints an absolute path; every
destructive fence starts with cd -- "${VAR:?...}" || exit 1 and checks it is
gstack's own checkout before any git command. /spec's worktree and spawn
fences get the same guard.

* F4: keep every paid design variant across regenerate rounds

$D variants now reserves a collision-safe round-<N>/ directory per run
(atomic mkdir) and writes a manifest.json of what each round saved. The
paid image request and the local write retry separately: a write failure
retries the write (temp + rename) and, if the path stays unwritable,
keeps the bytes in the temp dir instead of buying the image again.
Responsive variants land in their round directory too.

Readers updated: design-shotgun reserves a round dir and a private temp
dir for its parallel agents and records approved_path/round in
approved.json; design-html resolves approved_path (legacy letters still
work) and finds round-dir variants; design-consultation checks the
printed paths; the gallery shows round-dir variants. Variants that were
already overwritten before this change cannot be recovered.

Migrates the consultation contract test that pinned the flat path.

Co-authored-by: Matt Van Horn <mvanhorn@gmail.com>

* A2: stage dot-leading slugs gbrain can collect; network errors are db-unreachable

A page slug segment starting with a dot (a .claude project) staged a file
gbrain's import walker prunes, so the batch was refused on every run.
Leading dots become "dot-" per segment, and slugs recorded in state under
the old name map through the same function so no page is duplicated.

A DNS or connection failure (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNREFUSED, ...) no
longer classifies as broken-db, which routed users to move a working
config aside. The new db-unreachable status carries the reason
"database host unreachable (<code> <host>); your gbrain config is
unchanged. Fix: check network or VPN, then re-run /sync-gbrain.", skips
local sync stages with that reason, and counts as usable for
gstack-gbrain-detect --is-ok like timeout.

Co-authored-by: Infiniteyieldai <infiniteyield.ai@gmail.com>

* D2: one address classifier for navigation literals, DNS answers, redirects and page-driven navigations (#2811)

classifyAddress() in url-validation.ts blocks 169.254.0.0/16 (metadata and
container credential endpoints), 100.100.100.200, fe80::/10 and fc00::/7,
including IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible and NAT64 spellings and decimal,
octal and hex IPv4. validateNavigationUrl, the A/AAAA answer check and
session-persist's cookie-domain guard all use it. BrowserManager now checks
every navigation request (redirect hops, link clicks, scripted navigations):
a blocked target resets the tab to about:blank and the write command fails
with the reason. Connection-time DNS rebinding remains out of scope.

Co-authored-by: Gabriel Rondon <grondon@gmail.com>

* C4: external hosts point at carved sections relative to the installed skill

Publishes the pointer form setup matches: on every non-Claude host a carved
section is `sections/<file>` relative to the installed gstack-<skill> SKILL.md
directory (QA's existing form), never $GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections/, which
does not exist in external runtime roots. No render changes yet: only QA is
carved on external hosts today.

* INV-1: gate outcome contract for outside reviews

classifyOutsideReview() returns separate execution, findings and verdict
fields from text, stderr and exit status; reason codes, anchors and fix
actions live in lib/gate-outcomes.ts. validateOutsideReview() stays as the
text-only wrapper and the two-argument CLI keeps exit 0/1/2 for importers
and installed skills that predate a re-render. The --verdict form (implied
by --stderr/--exit) prints VERDICT/FINDINGS/REASON and exits 0/3/4/1; the
generated outside-voice caller moves to it and branches on each status
(unverified prints OUTSIDE_STATUS: unverified, never completed).

Adds docs/troubleshooting.md with one anchored section per reason code, the
anchor test, and the gate-tail lint (query scripts may not swallow failures,
gate calls may not end in || true, other best-effort tails say why).

* G1: quote the base placeholder in document-release title sync

The title-sync block is checked with bash -n; an unquoted <base> parses
as a redirection. Migrates the test that pinned the old root VERSION
read to the shared classifier call.

* G3: give every logging-bin mktemp a ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} template

Bare mktemp, mktemp -t and literal /tmp templates in the learnings,
question and preference logs (plus jsonl-merge, distill, the two
dashboards, /ship's PR body and /document-release's run dir) now use
"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>.XXXXXX", the form the INV-3 lint accepts. When
the temp file cannot be created, the learnings, question and preference
logs now say the entry was not recorded and how to fix TMPDIR instead of
exiting with only mktemp's own error. Three tests that pinned the bare
PR_BODY_FILE=$(mktemp) and one that pinned the /tmp run dir migrate.

GNU and BSD mktemp already honor TMPDIR without a template, so the
macOS-sandbox drop in #2952 is unverified here; the template makes the
temp location explicit on every mktemp.

Co-authored-by: Davon Johnson <d.johnson@dayofshow.net>

* B1b: structured outside-review gate fails on P0 as well as P1

validateOutsideReview() derived its structured pass/fail from a [P1] match,
so a review reporting only [P0] findings passed. The wrapper now reads the
classifier's findings verdict (P0 or P1), and the /review and /ship
structured-gate prose requests [P0]-[P3] tags and fails on P0/P1; untagged
output (OUTSIDE_STATUS: unverified) is missing coverage. The ship clarity
pin moves from 'structured P1' to 'structured P0/P1' with the behavior.

* E1: freeze normalizes boundary and target the same way on Windows; hooks spawn through cmd.exe (#2876, #2354)

gstack_hook_normalize_path (careful/bin/hook-extract.sh) maps C:\..., c:/...,
UNC \\server\share (leading // kept) and /cygdrive/c to one form; check-freeze
runs both the saved boundary and file_path through it before the absolute
test, after symlink resolution, and compares case-insensitively on Windows
bash. freeze, guard and careful register hooks as
bash -c "exec bash \"$HOME/...\"" so cmd.exe, which never expands $HOME,
no longer turns the hook into a silent exit 127.

Co-authored-by: Kevin Grasso <kevin@biblingo.com>
Co-authored-by: Xuan-Ce Wang <261591073+xwang4-svg@users.noreply.github.com>

* G4: keep CLI-to-daemon loopback calls off HTTP_PROXY (#494)

The CLI appends 127.0.0.1, localhost and ::1 to the user's NO_PROXY (and
no_proxy), keeping existing entries, before its first fetch. Verified on
Bun 1.4.0: fetch honors NO_PROXY when it is set before the first request
and ignores later changes, so it is set at the top of main().

* F1: bind the plan audit to this branch's plan, never the newest file

Plan File Discovery now prefers an explicit binding (the plan-mode file
or /autoplan ACTIVE_PLAN from the conversation, then a "Plan: <path>"
line in the PR body), then lists candidates: repo-committed
docs/designs/ files this branch changed or that name it, and personal
plan files that name the branch. Candidates are offered, never picked
silently. The repo-name match and the newest-file-of-the-day fallback,
which audited PRs against unrelated plans, are gone. With nothing bound
or chosen it prints the exact line 'Plan completion audit: not run (...).
Fix: add "Plan: <path>" to the PR body, or run /autoplan.'

/ship's parent now binds the plan before dispatching the audit
subagent ({{PLAN_COMPLETION_GATE_SHIP:discovery}}), so the child never
searches. Migrates three tests that pinned the old markers and notice.

Co-authored-by: loulanyue <260355617@qq.com>

* G5: browse type --selector <sel> <text> (#2936)

--selector focuses the element (sel or @ref) and types into it. The bare
form still types its text literally into the focused element; text that
starts with -- goes after a -- separator. When the first word looks like a
CSS selector, the result adds a hint to use --selector without echoing the
typed text, and never refuses based on page contents. Help and command
usage updated.

Co-authored-by: Thomas Reuser <thomasreuser@gmail.com>

* F2: design-doc discovery reads docs/designs, never a root DESIGN.md

A root DESIGN.md is the design system /design-consultation writes, so
preferring it unconditionally reviewed plans against a token file while
printing "Design doc found" and never looked at docs/designs/ feature
docs. Discovery now considers only docs/designs/*.md as the repo-local
design doc (still freshness-compared with the private ~/.gstack copy).
The CEO finding fixture seeds its supplied design as a docs/designs doc
and its test follows.

Co-authored-by: Bit0ps <alex.dreamscaper@gmail.com>

* C4: rename the external carve test (typecheck:test union-order artifact)

tsc prints a union's members in type-creation order; a test file sorting
before ceo-mode-option.test.ts reordered one baseline diagnostic's text.

* C1: every env-var host fence resolves its own gstack root

Codex and the other env-var hosts run each block in a fresh shell, so
GSTACK_ROOT/BIN, B and D set by the preamble were empty in later blocks
(/bin/gstack-slug, B=/browse). scripts/resolvers/runtime-root.ts now owns
root resolution: a valid exported GSTACK_ROOT (bin/ and lib/), else the
per-install literal root (no git call), else repo-local, else the global root
(CODEX_HOME on Codex); no root prints the setup fix line and exits. One
post-render pass inserts it (<=400 bytes) into every fence that uses these
variables without assigning them; B/D come from the same helper as BROWSE
and DESIGN SETUP. Claude output is byte-identical.

Migrated pins of the old preamble lines (gen-skill-docs.test.ts) and a
fixture whose exported GSTACK_ROOT lacked lib/ (skill-positional-literals).

* E8: headless browse honors GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH; extensions load in new headless mode (#2771, #1968, #2281)

The headless launch passes GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH as executablePath, scopes

Codex design and make-pdf skills fall back to $GSTACK_DESIGN and
$GSTACK_MAKE_PDF under the runtime root, but setup linked only browse/dist,

* C3: install router and nested SKILL.md files as real copies; back up hand edits; --status checks

Codex skips a symlinked SKILL.md file, so the gstack router linked into
~/.codex/skills/gstack was invisible. Every host runtime root (Codex,
Factory, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro) and Kiro's per-skill installs
now get real copies, rewritten on every run (the auto-update path runs
setup --refresh-registered, so it refreshes them too). setup records each
copy's hash in <state root>/skill-copies.tsv; a copy that no longer matches
is saved to a uniquely named backup under <state root>/backups/skill-copies/
before _activate_runtime_root replaces the tree, and a failed backup keeps
the old tree. setup prints what it refreshed or removed.

./setup --status now prints, per registered install, whether the router is a
real file and whether every section pointer resolves, with the fix command.

Test migration: setup-codex-model pinned the Kiro router/upgrade links as
_link_or_copy; C3 deliberately changes them to copies.

* INV-3: install-level host conformance checks (no symlinked SKILL.md, dist present, section pointers resolve)

For codex, kiro, factory, opencode, cursor and copilot, the real-setup
conformance kit now fails when an installed SKILL.md is a symlink, when
design/dist or make-pdf/dist is missing from the runtime root, or when a
'Read `.../sections/<f>.md`' pointer in an installed SKILL.md does not
resolve (bare pointers in carved skills, relative-to-installed-skill
pointers, and $GSTACK_ROOT/~/absolute/../ pointers everywhere), and
./setup --status must report 'all resolve'. No new setup runs.

Expected red until the generator lane lands: design-html's install-offer
pointer and plan-eng-review's review-sections pointer name
$GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections/... on every external host.

* B11: auto-update tracks pull, setup and migrations; announces only on success; retries with backoff

gstack-session-update wrote the 'just upgraded' marker after SETUP_FAILED or
SETUP_SKIPPED bun_missing, and re-ran setup only when HEAD moved, so a failed
install was announced as an upgrade and never retried. Stages are now
persisted in <state root>/session-update-pending; the marker is written only
when every stage succeeded; a pending setup or migrations stage is retried
even with HEAD unchanged after the update-check interval, then 6h, then 24h;
and each session start prints one line naming the stage, the reason and the
repair command while it is pending. Best-effort tails carry a same-line
reason.

* D1: gstack-config key browse_extension_id for forks and self-built extensions

The browse daemon trusts one Chrome extension ID on /extension-token and the
terminal-agent /ws. The override now lives only in gstack-config (never an
env var a project .env could set): empty by default (gstack's published
extension), a 32-letter a-p Chrome ID when set, "" clears it, and anything
else is rejected with the stored value kept. The browse lane reads it.

gstack-config-defaults: browse/src counts as a reader directory; the key is
listed prose-only until the browse lane's reader lands (the stale-entry check
then asks for the entry's removal).

* G2: key the sticky slug cache on the git common dir

A linked worktree used to resolve its slug fresh from the remote while
the main checkout kept its sticky pre-remote identity, so learnings,
checkpoints and timelines split into two buckets. gstack-slug and its
TS twin in lib/bin-context.ts now key the cache on the git common dir
(read from .git files, no git spawn, so cache hits stay git-free) and
read entries in one deterministic order: the repository entry, then the
main checkout's pre-upgrade entry, then this directory's own. Both the
repository and per-path entries are written.

When a worktree's own old entry named a different bucket that still
holds data, that slug is recorded in projects/<slug>/.former-slugs and
reported by --get FORMER_SLUGS. New --adopt-legacy --from <slug> merges
it: JSONL logs append missing lines with de-duplication, missing files
copy, differing files are listed as conflicts and never overwritten,
the source bucket is kept, and it prints migrated/pending/conflicting
counts; reruns are idempotent. --adopt-legacy --dismiss <slug> drops
the reminder.

* B1: Codex reviews whose sandbox could not start are unavailable, not a pass

In containers without unprivileged user namespaces every Codex command
fails, yet the review exits 0 and concludes 'no findings' (captured in
test/fixtures/codex-sandbox/). The validator now takes execution evidence:
'codex exec --json' command events and the 'codex review' stderr transcript
(a command that succeeded proves execution); sandbox failure lines on
stderr or in failed command output return unavailable(sandbox_unavailable);
exact 'could not run commands / read the diff' phrases are the last
fallback. Review text that merely discusses bwrap or namespaces still passes.

A free 'codex sandbox ... true' preflight (Linux, 10 s) runs before the paid
model probe and every automatic outside review; CODEX_MODE gains
sandbox_unavailable, and an inconclusive model probe reports unverified
instead of ready (exit code kept for stale callers). Every Codex site
(outside-voice resolver, /codex review, challenge, consult) takes its sandbox
from _GSTACK_CODEX_SANDBOX and pipes its result through the validator; a
static test parses rendered command positions for both. GSTACK_CODEX_NO_SANDBOX=1
(exactly 1, shell env only) switches to danger-full-access with a warning on
every use. Sandbox pins in existing tests move from the literal read-only to
the selected-sandbox variable; captured autoplan probes are judged against
the probe block they executed.

* C6: gstack-relink discovers skills structurally, so /browse survives a skill_prefix toggle

relink skipped a hardcoded list of support-directory names that included
browse, a real skill, so toggling skill_prefix removed /browse. A top-level
directory is now a skill exactly when it carries a SKILL.md.

* C4: carve ship and plan-ceo-review on every host; enforce the 160 KB byte gate

The generated ship skill was 202-241 KB on all 10 non-Claude hosts (and
Factory plan-ceo-review 160,039 bytes), over the 160,000-byte ceiling,
because section carving ran only for Claude. Both skills now carve on every
host, pointing at sections relative to the installed skill directory (literal
$GSTACK_ROOT/<skill>/sections refs are rewritten the same way). The ceiling
is measured in UTF-8 bytes and fails generation in repo mode; under
--install-root it warns so setup never leaves a user without skills.

qa-lazy-sections.test.ts pinned ship as inline-on-external-hosts; migrated to
the carved policy and kept the inline check on review (Claude-only carve).

* B5: learnings and timeline reads fail loudly when bun is missing

gstack-learnings-search and gstack-timeline-read ended in
'2>/dev/null || exit 0', so a missing bun or a crashed embedded script
printed nothing and exited 0, identical to 'nothing recorded'. Both now
exit 127 with '<script>: bun not found on PATH, so ... could not be
read. Fix: install Bun (https://bun.sh), then re-run ./setup.' and let
an embedded-script failure exit non-zero with its stderr. A successful
run with no matches still exits 0 with empty output. The generated
callers that print 'LEARNINGS: unavailable (...)' belong to the
generator lane.

* B2: a retired-model 404 reports MODEL_UNUSABLE, not CODEX_MODE: ready

The model probe matched only 400 / 'is not supported', so a retired model's
404 ('does not exist or you do not have access to it') and a custom
provider's bare 404 fell through to the inconclusive branch and reported
ready. Both now classify as MODEL_UNUSABLE with a hint naming the two causes
(retired model, or a wrong base_url) and log codex_model_retired; a
'requires a newer version of Codex' 400 points at upgrading the CLI and logs
codex_cli_outdated. Ported from #2843 onto the current probe.

Co-authored-by: Marek Cermak <marek.cermak@strv.com>

* B6: rank learnings by matched query tokens and disclose truncation

A more specific query used to drop the exact match: the token-OR filter
recalled every entry sharing one token, the sort used confidence alone,
and the default --limit cut silently. Entries now rank by how many
distinct query tokens they match, then confidence, then recency, and a
query that matched more than fit says '-- N more matched, raise --limit
to see them'. The hit count lives in a local map so a field stored on
disk can never become a sort key, and the type grouping uses a
null-prototype map so a row typed 'constructor' or '__proto__' cannot
crash the run. Ranking code ported from #2796; regression vectors
adapted from #2799 (its stemmer is not needed).

Copilot CLI applies Claude-format matchers by tool name; its skill tool is
`skill`, which no Claude tool name maps to, so the 'Skill' matcher never
fired and Copilot ran protected skills without gstack. The hook entry now
matches 'Skill|skill', an entry an older team-init wrote is upgraded in

* B3: Codex auth probe accepts custom providers' env_key credentials

The auth probe only knew CODEX_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and auth.json, so a
working self-hosted or OpenAI-compatible provider configured with
[model_providers.<id>] env_key = "X" reported AUTH_FAILED and /codex
